cohort_name: unnamed: Poona Hospital (Pune) and Manasdeep Centre (Ahmednagar) private psychiatric outpatient SMI cohort
diagnostic_instrument: medical record diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder or major depression; no research diagnostic interview
diagnosis_confirmed: medical record diagnosis only, taken from the treating service
overlap_notes: Baseline assessment of this same cohort is reported by Khare et al. 2020, cited throughout and not staged in this batch. NOT the same cohort as pune_public (khare2022 / unknown2022), which is a public-sector sample.
employment_selection_verbatim: Inclusion criteria were: 1) medical record diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or major depression; 2) age 18-60 years old; 3) verbally fluent in Marathi language; 4) residing in Pune or Ahmednagar districts and receiving outpatient treatment at one of the two hospitals; and 5) willing and able to provide informed consent. | Baseline employment was measured, not required: 278 of the 456 analysed participants (60.9 per cent of the 550 baseline sample) were working at baseline, so the substantial majority of the non-working were retained. | Note recorded and considered: 'Two participants who completed the follow-up reported being full-time students and one reported working as a volunteer. These participants were excluded from the analyses, leaving 456 participants for the final analyses.' That removes 3 of 459 on activity status at FOLLOW-UP as a construct-boundary decision, not on baseline employment, so it is not read as employment-related selection under D9; it is recorded here so a checker can disagree.
employment_selection_source: Methods 2.1 Participants, p. 473; Methods 2.2 Procedures, p. 473; Results 3 and 3.1, p. 474; Table 1, p. 475

cohort_name: Compassionate Recovery: Individualised Support in early Psychosis (CR:ISP) study
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 diagnosis of non-organic psychosis; PANSS for symptoms
diagnosis_confirmed: clinical ICD-10 diagnosis at first presentation to mental health services
overlap_notes: The training dataset of leighton2019b. The same participants are inside leighton2019's pooled 'Scottish' validation sample of 162, from which no result is taken.
employment_selection_verbatim: The Compassionate Recovery: Individualised Support in early Psychosis (CR:ISP) study was a 24-month non-randomised prospective study of individuals with FEP... Recruitment took place in mental health services in the NHS Greater Glasgow & Clyde (NHSGGC) health board between 2011 and 2014. To be considered for inclusion participants had to be: (a) in-patients or out-patients with (b) first presentation to mental health services for psychosis, (c) ICD-10 diagnosis of non-organic psychosis. 83 participants were entered into the study. | Baseline EET was measured, not required: 'Employment, Education or Training - No. (%) 45 (56)' at baseline, so 36 of 81 with the item were not in EET at entry and were retained.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants and study design, p. 3; Table 1, p. 6

diagnostic_instrument: not stated in leighton2019b; PANSS for symptoms, BDI-II for depression
diagnosis_confirmed: not stated in leighton2019b; described previously in Gumley et al. 2014, Br J Psychiatry 205:60-67

employment_selection_verbatim: The validation dataset was formed of 79 FEP patients recruited to an earlier study (1 September 2006 to 31 August 2009), which took place in mental health services in the NHS in Glasgow and in Edinburgh. Participants and study design have been described previously (see S1 File). | That is the whole of what the article prints about eligibility for this cohort: no inclusion or exclusion criteria are given, so absence of an employment-related restriction cannot be established and D9 requires unclear. S1 File and Gumley et al. 2014 would resolve it and neither is held. | Baseline EET was measured, not required: 'Employment, Education or Training - No. (%) 40 (52)'.

cohort_name: unnamed: Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University childhood-onset schizophrenia first-admission cohort, 2000-2013
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 criteria for schizophrenia, age of first onset 14 years or younger
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnosed after full physical, neurological, laboratory and imaging work-up by a chief or associate chief physician and an attending physician; admission diagnosis sustained at discharge; retrospective diagnostic re-evaluation by two experienced clinicians from the medical records, which removed 11 patients whose diagnosis had changed
employment_selection_verbatim: The sample included 276 patients, age of first onset 14 years old or less, fulfilling the criteria for schizophrenia according to the ICD-10, and admitted to the Department of Psychiatry at the Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University for the first time, between January 2000 and December 2013. | 'The inclusion criteria for this study include the age of first onset 14 years old or less, fulfilling the criteria for schizophrenia according to the ICD-10, no comorbidities, no primary organic mental disorder, no drug and/or alcohol-induced psychosis, and no intellectual disability.' | The criteria are printed in full and contain no employment-related restriction. Loss of 106 of 276 to follow-up is attrition, which under D12.3c is not employment selection.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants, p. 2; Figure 1 footnote a, p. 2; Table 2 footnote a, p. 4

diagnostic_instrument: BPRS Expanded Version 4.0 at entry (psychosis defined as a score of 4 or more for unusual thought content or hallucinations); SCID for DSM-IV Research Version at 2 and 12 months
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnoses set by a senior psychiatrist on all available information, with mental health treatment records used to complement the SCID interview
employment_selection_verbatim: The FEP group consisted of adults making their first psychiatric treatment contact for psychosis, recruited to the Helsinki Early Psychosis Study from hospitals and outpatient clinics of the city of Helsinki and Helsinki University Hospital. They were interviewed with the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS), Expanded Version 4.0, as soon as possible after they had commenced treatment and were able to provide informed consent, as judged by the treating personnel. As an inclusion criterion, psychosis was defined as a score of 4 or more (moderate or higher) for unusual thought content or hallucinations. Exclusion criteria were psychotic disorders that were substance induced or caused by a general medical condition. | The eligibility criteria are printed in full and carry no employment-related restriction. Restriction of the analysed sample to those with both baseline cognitive data and 1-year clinical data is data availability, that is attrition under D12.3c, not employment selection.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants, p. 2; Results, p. 3; Table 1, p. 4

cohort_name: unnamed: Changsha Assertive Community Treatment randomised controlled trial (ChiCTR-TRC-13003407)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV diagnosis of schizophrenia; SCID-II to exclude personality disorder; SCID-I/NP applied to co-residing family members
diagnosis_confirmed: DSM-IV diagnosis confirmed by clinical assessment and chart review
employment_selection_verbatim: The inclusion criteria for patients were: (1) age 18-45 years; (2) diagnosis of schizophrenia based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders-Fourth Edition (DSM-IV); (3) no organic brain disorder, mental retardation, severe head trauma, or personality disorder; (4) significant functional impairment; (5) have one or more indicators of a need for continuous high level of services [criteria for (4) and (5) were based on standard ACT Manual description (Allness and Knoedler, 2003) and confirmed by clinical assessment, see details in the online Supplementary materials]; (6) no co-residing family member with a mental illness; and (7) both the patient and a co-residing family caregiver provide written informed consent to participate. | No employment criterion is printed. Two things stop this being coded none. First, the operational content of criteria (4) and (5) is held only in the online Supplementary materials, which are not in the PDF held, and the ACT admission criteria they derive from customarily include inability to obtain or maintain employment. Second, the outcome is framed throughout as RE-employment, with every participant at risk from day 0 of a Kaplan-Meier analysis 'censored at 365 days if the event did not occur', which implies that none of the analysed sample was in paid work at baseline. Neither is stated, so this is unclear on incomplete reporting rather than selected. | The triage hint 'selected for severe impairment' is refuted as a ground: severe functional impairment is not one of the employment-related criteria D9 enumerates.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study population and recruitment, p. 970; Study outcomes and data collection, p. 972; Statistical analysis, p. 972; online Supplementary materials NOT HELD
